findings.text: blocking: the new "ingested" ResetSpec sets source_filter="n.relevance_stage = 'content'", which reset_to_status renders as `n.status IN $source_statuses OR (n.relevance_stage = 'content')`. Because the clause is OR-ed with the status match, the reset admits EVERY content-stage CodeFile regardless of status: a probe (reset-predicate probe, reviewed tree) shows the rendered predicate admits scored, skipped and triaged content-stage files, and the reset then SETs their status='ingested' and nulls their judgment fields facility-wide. The plan scopes the pass to the ingested files that carry no facet answer and states the content reset already handles scored and skipped; this single run would demote and clear the whole facility's content-stage corpus. A correct reach needs an AND restriction (the reset's extra_filter "AND n.relevance_stage = 'content'"), not the OR-widening source_filter.

follow-on: the fragment claims the reset "scopes to relevance_stage = 'content' at ingested, so the 12 files that already carry an answer are not re-asked". This is not borne by the code: the first disjunct `n.status IN ['ingested']` matches all 552 ingested content-stage files, so the reset clears the 12 answered files' score_data_access_confidence too, defeating the claim's own drain key coalesce(score_data_access_confidence,0)=0 — every ingested content-stage file is re-asked, not just the 540.

follow-on: test_code_ingested_reset_renders_content_stage_predicate asserts the widened predicate string "n.status IN $source_statuses OR (n.relevance_stage = 'content')" is rendered, so the test guards the over-reach rather than catching it; the node's only firing negative control exercises the chunk-text guard, leaving the reset behaviour unguarded.
